To solve the problem, we need to determine why the C-H bond in acetylenes is more reactive compared to typical hydrocarbons.

Acetylenes, also known as alkynes, have a carbon-carbon triple bond. This triple bond consists of one sigma bond and two pi bonds. The presence of these pi bonds makes the hydrogen atoms in acetylenes more acidic compared to those in alkanes or alkenes. The increased acidity of the hydrogen atoms in acetylenes is due to the fact that the sp hybridized carbon, which holds the hydrogen, is more electronegative and can stabilize the negative charge better when the hydrogen is removed as a proton.

Thus, the correct answer to why the C-H bond in acetylenes is more reactive is because of the acidic nature of the hydrogens due to the sp hybridized carbon.
